items.summary: Depuis 2 mois, les feux de forêt se multiplient en Indonésie. La faute au réchauffement climatique mais pas seulement. L'Indonésie subit les conséquences d'un El Niño très intense qui entraîne sur place un climat chaud et sec, favorable aux incendies. La gestion des forêts indonésiennes est aussi fautive: des parcelles rasées pour planter des monocultures de palmiers à huile notamment, très inflammables, ou des tourbières asséchées pour cultiver les sols.

Milton College was ahead of its time in admitting women. It was a coeducational institution from the start. items.title: [Editorial] Rethinking lived experience
items.summary: The theme of this year's World Mental Health Day, held on Oct 10, is Lived experiences heard: real voices, real change. On its website, WHO states that the voices of people with lived experience should “shape the policies, services and decisions that affect their lives”. While these are laudable aims, they also serve to highlight the complex challenges involved in lived experience engagement and co-production, both within the field of mental health and beyond.

items.title: [Comment] Retatrutide in adults with obesity and type 2 diabetes: what have we learned from TRIUMPH-2?
items.summary: It is a general observation that the degree of weight loss obtained with GLP-1 receptor agonists is less in individuals with type 2 diabetes than in people without diabetes and similar BMI. Could this difference be overcome with the new triple agonists with superior weight-lowering effects? The TRIUMPH-2 study by Virginia Bellido and colleagues1 in The Lancet is a double-blind, parallel-group, randomised, placebo-controlled, phase 3 trial of the effects of retatrutide, a triple agonist (GLP-1, GIP, and glucagon), in people with obesity and type 2 diabetes.

items.title: [Comment] Closing the gap on mortality for adolescents living with HIV

items.title: [Comment] Offline: Medicine for peace
items.summary: Thomas Hobbes (1588–1679) is most famous for his line in Leviathan (1651) that, “the life of man, solitary, poor, nasty, brutish, and short”. That proposition may have been true in 17th-century England, but, thanks to the evolution and expansion of health systems, it is not so today for many, although obviously not all. But abstracting that line alone is to miss Hobbes’ wider views about the nature of human being. He believed that without a “common power” ruling over society, our natural tendency is “that condition which is called war…of every man against every man”.

items.title: [Correspondence] Regulate prospective development of medical AI now
items.summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) is advancing through medicine at a pace that regulation, ethics, and professional reflection have struggled to match. The prevailing assumption appears to be that if a technology can be developed, it should be developed—and that its place in clinical care can be debated afterwards. We believe this sequence should be reversed.

items.title: [Correspondence] The health literacy crisis in the age of AI: lessons from PISA 2025
items.summary: The 2025 Programme for International Student Assessment (PISA) results should concern the health community.1 PISA does not measure health literacy directly, but it assesses several cognitive competencies that increasingly underpin people's ability to navigate health information. For example, in 2025, more than 760 000 students aged 15 years, from 91 countries and economies, participated in the assessment.1 The findings reveal a worrying deterioration in reading, mathematics, and science performance.

items.title: [Correspondence] Taiwan's path to hepatitis C elimination
items.summary: WHO has established a global target to eliminate viral hepatitis as a public health threat by 2030.1 Chronic hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection remains one of the leading causes of cirrhosis, hepatocellular carcinoma, and liver-related mortality, affecting an estimated 50 million people worldwide.2 By integrating a comprehensive screening-to-cure cascade, HCV elimination has become an achievable public health goal.

items.title: [Correspondence] Personalising maintenance after tirzepatide weight loss
items.summary: Deborah B Horn and colleagues’ SURMOUNT-MAINTAIN trial provides important evidence that continued tirzepatide is superior to treatment withdrawal for maintaining pharmacologically induced weight loss.1 The trial also shows that reducing tirzepatide to 5 mg offers substantially greater protection against weight regain than switching to placebo. However, the trial's mean effects might not fully convey an important clinical message: response to lower-dose maintenance was heterogeneous.

items.title: [Correspondence] How much can ASTRUM-006 tell us?
items.summary: Lin Shen and colleagues report improved event-free survival with perioperative serplulimab in PD-L1-positive resectable gastric or gastro-oesophageal junction adenocarcinoma.1 The trial is valuable: it selects patients by combined positive score and tests a chemotherapy-free adjuvant phase. However, we urge caution before it is read as practice-changing.

items.title: [Correspondence] How much can ASTRUM-006 tell us? – Authors’ reply
items.summary: We thank Osman Bilge Kaya and Berkan Karabuğa for their insightful comments regarding ASTRUM-006.1 We agree that some aspects need further clarification.

items.title: [Correspondence] Colonoscopy screening and colorectal cancer outcomes: the NordICC trial
items.summary: Michal F Kaminski and colleagues report that colonoscopy screening reduced colorectal cancer incidence, but not mortality, during a 13-year follow-up.1 The response from the public health field will focus, as it always does, on mortality. We think this focus misses the point of the trial.

items.title: [Correspondence] Colonoscopy screening and colorectal cancer outcomes: the NordICC trial
items.summary: In their recent Article, Michal F Kaminski and colleagues reported the effects of offering one-time screening colonoscopy at ages 55–64 years after a 13-year follow-up of the NordICC trial.1 Their findings should be interpreted in the context that this trial of a one-time offer of screening colonoscopy was conducted in an era of widespread use of colonoscopy in clinical practice. Estimated reductions in the incidence and mortality of colorectal cancer were much lower than anticipated at trial design.

items.title: [Correspondence] Colonoscopy screening and colorectal cancer outcomes: the NordICC trial
items.summary: The NordICC trial1 should be considered in context with previous colorectal cancer screening studies.2,3 Four randomised controlled trials with more than 458 000 participants show consistent colorectal cancer incidence reductions of 18–23% and larger colorectal cancer mortality reductions of 22–31% with sigmoidoscopy (appendix).3 In the NordICC trial, screening reduced colorectal cancer incidence but not mortality.1

items.summary: The Wood Street Steps are the last surviving examples of 10 or more stairways Philadelphia founder William Penn commissioned along the original Delaware Riverbank. Why are they important? Penn felt all citizens should have public access to the river wharves. Some early wealthy Quakers, who owned land there, disagreed. As part of a 1684 compromise, Penn made sure at least 10 stairways led to the port area near major cross streets ... from Vine Street to what was originally called Cedar Street ... and is now known as South Street. Unfortunately, this is the only set of those steps left.

items.title: [Review] Machine learning prediction for epilepsy treatment selection and prognosis: achievements and challenges
items.summary: Accurate prediction of treatment response and selection of optimal treatments remain challenging in epilepsy management. With no reliable surrogate biomarkers for treatment response, the current process of selecting an antiseizure medication remains largely a trial-and-error approach. Other non-pharmacological treatment options, such as epilepsy surgery, are viable alternatives for patients with drug-resistant epilepsy. Statistical and machine learning techniques have been used to predict seizure outcomes associated with antiseizure medications and epilepsy surgery.
